summary: The article argues that community college adult learning programs have become essential in a changing economy, supporting lifelong learning, career change, and local workforce needs. It covers inclusivity, economic gains, skills-gap partnerships with employers, well-being benefits, pandemic-era adaptability, and the case for government funding. Quotes from educators, an alumnus, an IT specialist, a psychologist, and a legislator support these points.
one_line: Community college adult learning programs drive lifelong learning, economic empowerment, skills-gap bridging, and well-being, and merit stronger policy and funding support.
key_facts: The article is dated September 30, 2023 and is filed under the topic Local Education Systems.
Tom Jackson, an educational researcher, says, "The workers of today need to be learners tomorrow."
Recent studies cited show nearly half of all employment sectors now require continuing education for career advancement.
Dr. Maria Torres, a dean at Greenview Community College, says the college runs evening and weekend classes, online and hybrid courses, and targeted support services for adults.

A report released on October 12, 2023 by the National Bureau for Education Statistics found a direct correlation between adult learning participation and increased earnings, decreased reliance on social services, and improved job stability.
James McArthur, an alumnus of Clearwater Community College's adult education program, moved into a career in cybersecurity; two years earlier he was working odd jobs.
Community colleges work closely with local businesses and industries to offer courses aligned with job market needs, and employers actively participate in curriculum development.
Methods used to bridge the skills gap include skills-based courses, apprenticeships, and on-the-job training.
Jennifer Levine, a health psychologist and professor at the local state university, says lifelong learning reduces stress and increases life satisfaction.

Steven Kim, an IT specialist at Riverside Community College, facilitated the rapid move of curriculums online and trained instructors and students on digital platforms during the global health crisis.
State Representative Lisa Grant advocates increased funding, saying adult education is integral to community prosperity and should be prioritized in the budget.
The article says funding, grants, and subsidies are essential for removing access barriers to adult education.
